subject: Transient handoffs, execution loci, and deletion timelines
messages:

Subject: Clarify processing footprint and deletion SLAs for PH pilot

Hi Sean,

Thanks for the demo yesterday. Legal asked me to follow up with a few concrete questions so we can move the pilot through our procurement checklist. Can you confirm the following?

1) Where exactly are inference requests executed for the hosted API (region list + common transient hops)? We need to know whether requests originating in the EU could traverse US-based infra at any point.
2) For accounts that require EU-only processing, what deployment options enforce that guarantee (hosted pin, dedicated capacity, private VPC)?
3) Evidence we can share with our auditors: an architecture/process map showing regions and subprocessors; the current subprocessor roster; and the deletion/erasure timelines for AI inputs, model artifacts, and operational logs.

Also: what are typical retention windows for ephemeral logs and backups, and what's the SLA for on-demand erasure requests?

If you can send a short written Q&A plus any attachments, that would be ideal. Our timeline is tight — procurement wants materials before EOW.

Best,
Irina

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Clarify processing footprint and deletion SLAs for PH pilot

Hi Irina — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers below; I'm attaching a short processing map and the subprocessor CSV in my next message (we have a SOC 2 infra excerpt too). Happy to jump on a quick call if you want to walk through these.

Summary (hosted API):
- Execution loci: primary EU regions are eu-west-1 (Dublin) and eu-central-1 (Frankfurt). For most EU-origin traffic we route to the nearest EU POP; however, in rare capacity or connectivity failover events, requests may be routed to a compatible model in a nearby non-EU region (e.g., us-west-2) unless the tenant is pinned.
- Transient hops: prefix/KV cache replication and some control-plane actions may cause metadata to traverse other regions (these are transient and encrypted in transit). We do not persist customer prompt/response payloads outside the execution region for pinned/dedicated tenants.
- EU-only guarantee: two viable options: Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool in an EU region) or Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) — both enforce EU-only execution and do not perform cross-border fallbacks. Hosted self-serve accounts can request an EU-pin but that is treated as a tenancy preference rather than a guaranteed legal boundary; we can discuss contractual language if required.

Deletion and retention (defaults and options):
- On-demand erasure request (customer-facing): we start purge within 24 hours; tokens and short-lived caches are removed and dependent indexes are updated; completion confirmation within 30 days for hosted accounts.
- Ephemeral inference logs: default retention is 90 days for hosted accounts (used for debugging and SLO analysis); Dedicated/Private can have custom policies (30–90 days typical).
- Backups and snapshots: up to 365 days by default for multi-zone resiliency; can be reduced with contract.
- Model artifacts: model binaries and versions are treated as infra artifacts (not customer data). Customer prompts/outputs are deleted per the retention window or on-demand erasure.

I'll loop in the operations and legal folks internally to provide the attachments and a short statement for your auditors.

Regards,

- redwood_processing_map_q1_2028.pdf (diagram showing execution regions, common prefix cache replication patterns, and failover behavior)
- subprocessor_inventory_20280110.csv (current list: regional cloud infra providers, log storage, observability vendors; includes contact/residence columns)
- soc2_section_infra_excerpt.pdf (excerpt describing control of data-in-transit and change management)

Suggested legal-safe sentence for Dedicated/Private: 
"When provisioned as Redwood Dedicated in an EU region or deployed via Redwood Private in your VPC located in the EU, Polaris Health data is executed and persisted only within the specified EU region(s); Redwood will not failover execution to non-EU regions for that tenant, and we will include this commitment in the contract's data residency clause."

On-demand erasure SLA: 
- Hosted: ingestion artifacts, caches, and customer-visible indexes — purge initiated within 24 hours; verification/reporting completed within 30 days.
- Dedicated: purge initiated within 24 hours; verification/reporting completed within 10 business days (operational access to instance-level control).

Notes on transient metadata: control-plane metadata (routing telemetry, anonymized metrics) may traverse other regions for routing/monitoring; we encrypt in transit (TLS + mTLS) and minimize retention. If Polaris needs full avoidance of cross-border metadata, Private deployment is the recommended path.

Hi Irina — attaching the materials Marissa prepared (processing map, subprocessor inventory, SOC 2 excerpt). Short answers inlined below to make review easier for your auditors: 

- Execution regions: eu-west-1 (Dublin), eu-central-1 (Frankfurt) are our primary EU POPs. We also operate additional EU edge POPs for latency-sensitive routing.
- Transient hops: For our default hosted offering, transient failover to non-EU regions can occur during capacity or connectivity events; metadata for routing/observability is minimized and encrypted.
- EU-only guarantee: Redwood Dedicated (EU-region reservation) and Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) both provide contractual EU-only execution guarantees; we included a suggested clause in the attached doc.
- Deletion/erasure: Hosted: purge initiated within 24 hours, completion confirmation within 30 days. Dedicated: purge completion confirmation within 10 business days. Ephemeral inference logs: default 90-day retention for hosted; configurable on Dedicated/Private. Backups: up to 365 days by default; can be amended in contract.

Attachments: redwood_processing_map_q1_2028.pdf, subprocessor_inventory_20280110.csv, soc2_section_infra_excerpt.pdf
